name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that follows tab order—no exceptions. This guarantees keyboard users always see where they are, which is non-negotiable for accessibility. The trade-off is visual noise for sighted keyboard users, but that’s a worthwhile cost for universal usability.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s single ring overloads sighted keyboard users—cognitive noise rises with long lists, and a 250 ms delay can still drop the ring between tabs at 125 ms. Instead, pair a subtle, persistent ring with a 50 ms flash on first focus; sighted users learn the ring’s location without constant glare, while screen-reader users still get clear feedback. Settle it with a quick A/B test: measure task completion time and error rate for 10 keyboard users—if the flash version wins, adopt it.
